reconcile.note: Gill reads Matthew's second cry as encompassing both Luke's and John's sayings, treating the three last words as sequential rather than mutually exclusive.

discrepancy.note: Strauss holds that each evangelist gives his own distinct dying words for Jesus rather than a shared sequence.

quotes.text: Concerning the last words which the expiring Jesus was heard to utter, the Evangelists differ. … while according to John it was on the brief expression: it is finished
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), ch. on the crucifixion, on Matthew 27:46 and John 19:30.

sides.snippet: \"Eli, Eli, lima sabachthani?\" That is, \"My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?\"
sides.verseText: About the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, \"Eli, Eli, lima sabachthani?\" That is, \"My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?\"

sides.snippet: he said, \"It is finished.\" He bowed his head, and gave up his spirit.
sides.verseText: When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, \"It is finished.\" He bowed his head, and gave up his spirit.
